idea: Financial model building and maintenance for small funds
buyer: Small funds and family offices without junior analysts
pain: Nobody to build and maintain models; PM time wasted in spreadsheets
v1: Build one company model to their template
verdict: Fast and easy to sell, but low price and pure hours make the ceiling hard.

why.distribution: Her exact peer group, immediately reachable, and the ask is small enough to say yes to.
why.demand: Outsourced modelling is a real market, though no one here has been asked for money.
why.fmf: Eight years of building exactly these models to institutional standard.
why.revenue_structure: Repeat purchase without contract; maintenance retainers possible but not the default.
why.defensibility: Rebuildable by any competent analyst, and increasingly by the buyer with an LLM.
why.leverage: Templates help, but revenue still tracks hours worked.
why.time_to_revenue: Sellable this month to someone she knows.
why.tailwind: Actively adverse - this is the single task LLMs are absorbing fastest.
why.ceiling: £2.5k x 40 models = £100k, and 40 models a year part-time is not realistic.

ceiling_arithmetic: £2.5k x 40 models = £100k at full tilt; realistically 15-20 models part-time = £40-50k. Price is too low and the hours too high to reach the target.
carries: Trivially easy to start and sell; useful as a wedge into a relationship.
kills: Ceiling and tailwind together. It is the task most exposed to AI absorption, at the lowest price point.
test: Offer two PMs a model build at £2k.
test_pass: Both accept and ask about ongoing maintenance.
test_fail: They say their junior or ChatGPT does it.
